page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores via hyperthreading, utilizing Intel Xeon 8573C processors operating at frequencies up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Compute benchmarks show solid single-core and multi-core throughput, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 2110.0 and a multi-core score of 16603.0, both placing in the upper quartile.

Memory allocation is heavily prioritized, featuring 512.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 16.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration provides a high memory-to-core ratio suited for large in-memory footprints. For local I/O requirements, the instance bundles 3780 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD storage, eliminating reliance on network storage for temporary files and local persistence. However, PassMark memory testing registers in the lower quartile at 1572.37, and uncached large-block memory write speeds reach 74.71 GB/sec, suggesting that workloads requiring high sustained memory write bandwidth across the entire array should account for this characteristic.

Without hardware acceleration like discrete GPUs, raw large-model execution is constrained, as demonstrated by 70B parameter LLM text generation throughput of 2.45 tokens per second. Smaller models perform substantially better, reaching 296.69 tokens per second on lightweight text generation. The high RAM density and fast bundled NVMe make the E64-32ds_v6 cost-efficient for core-licensed software and memory-heavy workloads, including enterprise in-memory databases, large Redis deployments, analytical caches, and big data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine offering 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores running at 4.2 GHz. Equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an extensive 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 260 MB of L3 cache and support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. The server includes 3780 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage to support high-throughput temporary and scratch operations. Geekbench benchmarking highlights strong processing capabilities with scores of 2110.0 single-core and 16603.0 multi-core, while Redis benchmarks indicate 44.76 million SET operations per second. Lacking discrete GPUs, large-scale inference is limited, but the constrained vCPU count alongside high memory makes this instance cost-effective for core-licensed relational databases, in-memory caching systems, and intensive enterprise analytical workloads.
